data.name: Delta Force: Task Force Dagger
data.detailed_description:
As the US army's elite special operations soldiers you are the most potent 'smart weapon' known to man. You are the 'tip of the spear' for covert operations around the world — you are the first line of attack. Nothing stands in your way. From the war torn streets of Somalia you have been re-deployed to take out targets in Colombia and Iran. As the US military's preemptive strike force you must work with your team to get the job done.

Features

  • BECOME THE BEST — Play as any one of these Special Forces units: SFOD-Delta, 2/75th RANGER, SEAL Team 6, SFOD-SF Viper Team (Green Berets), CIA Special Operations, UK SAS 22 Regiment, Australian SASR, Canadian JTF-2, Marines Force Recon, and USAF CSAR (Air Force Pararescue) — all the actual Special Forces units deployed in Operation Enduring Freedom.
  • INFILTRATE ACTUAL LOCATIONS — 25 new Delta Force missions! Take over the Kandahar Airport, raid rebel headquarters in Mazar-e-Sharif, ambush a convoy near the Pakistani border and demolish bunkers in the foothills of Kabul.
  • OVER 30 WEAPONS TO CHOOSE FROM — Gear up with a huge arsenal of machine guns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, pistols and rocket launchers new to the Delta Force series.
  • SPY ON THE ENEMY — Plan your attack with the element of surprise using visual intelligence gathered from Unmanned Aerial Vehicles.
  • RAIN DESTRUCTION FROM THE SKIES — Call in devastating air strikes to take out key SAM and SCUD missile sites.
  • LARGE-SCALE MULTIPLAYER — Create your own multiplayer games and maps with the mission editor. 10 new multiplayer maps included! *Battle online via NovaWorld.

reviews.review:
“Delta Force – Task Force Dagger” is the 4th instalment of the tactical first-person-shooter series. At the time of its release in 2002, the game design, sounds and graphics were already hopelessly outdated and critics at the time were wondering how the developers could be so audacious to release the game at nearly AAA title pricing. 

After about 7,2 hours in a completionist approach, here’s my pros/cons list:

Pros: 
+ slightly improved graphics compared to “DF – Land Warrior”
+ improved weapon models

Cons:
-	weapon models cut off (they’re 2D pictures), can be seen during jumps
-	slow, inaccurate mouse aim
-	objectives are shown only after you enter a mission, instead of showing them during mission briefing
-	close quarters combat pretty bad
-	one shot even with a silenced weapon will many times alert all enemies on the map
-	enemies can see through walls
-	static sound direction
-	enemy footstep sounds missing mostly
-	terrible climbing ladders
-	even worse clipping issues
-	checkpoint update issues
-	sometimes hard to find objectives like files, missing highlight or marker in HUD or on map
-	teammates AI is so stupid it’s practically useless
-	repetitive campaign missions
-	lots of map recycling
-	racist depictions of Afghan people
-	missing modern keyboard / controls setup
-	keyboard needs pause key to pause mission, instead of using the ESC-button to get to a menu as was the long-standing standard already back then
-	maximum resolution still only at 1024x768
-	jumping down ledges or walking down mountains feels like the game has moon gravity
-	many graphic glitches
-	strange Kabul mission
-	very strange menu music
-	missing description of each playable character’s strengths, despite the fact that they do have major differences
-	Pakistani border mission practically impossible to win due to its setup
-	super stretched, boring, repetitive Tora Bora mission

Conclusion: 
Probably the worst of all Delta Force games, hopelessly outdated at the time of its release and overall very boring, repetitive with quite a few bugs which are existing until today, 24 years later. Recommended only for hardcore nostalgic fans. 

Rating: 3/10 points
